text:
Mina K.: FYI acme-corp just opened a P1 — streaming responses intermittently contain extra trailing text, JSON.parse fails in their consumer. Happened ~3x in last hour. Request IDs: r-ff12, r-ff13.
Ashok: Can you paste the raw response snippet (including the streaming trailer)? often it's a single rogue token or a repeated newline.
Mina K.: Pasted below (redacted):
```
...
}
}
Oops: extra-debug-info

--- END STREAM ---
```
Sasha: ugh. That looks like the model appended debug text after the final `}`. Two quick options: 1) re-ask / strict JSON guard, 2) post-process sanitizer that strips trailing garbage.
Jamie: For re-ask pattern we recommend: on parse failure do up to 2 quick re-asks with exponential backoff (200ms -> 600ms) and a stricter system instruction: `Please respond only with a single JSON object that strictly matches the schema and nothing else.` Add `If you cannot, return exactly: ERROR: <reason>`.
Kevin: Example pseudo-flow we use in support:
```
1) attempt parse
2) if parse fails -> re-ask prompt: "You returned invalid JSON. Please reply ONLY with valid JSON matching schema X. If you cannot, reply ERROR: <reason>."
3) retry <= 2 times with backoff (200ms, 600ms)
4) if still fails -> try sanitizer regex and a non-stream sync call fallback
```
Ashok: Sanitizer regex we include in client libs: find the last `}` and take substring up to that char, or use a greedy match like `r"(\{[\s\S]*\})"` to extract the biggest JSON-looking chunk. That covers most trailing-text cases but is brittle for truncated JSON.
Mina K.: Customer is on streaming mode and cannot tolerate 2s latency. We should be careful with extra re-asks. Any lower-latency mitigations?
Sasha: Short term: 1) switch their route to non-streaming for critical endpoints so they get a single complete payload (often avoids trailer corruption), 2) enable proxy-level sanitizer that trims after the last balanced brace before returning to the client. Both are quick config changes.
Jamie: Also check the model / checkpoint: we've seen a specific quantized variant occasionally append free-text; ask Eng-ML to check model-variant rtx-q8 logs if repeated.
Kevin: If you escalate to eng-runtime include: sample request payload, model name & variant, full raw stream, request_id(s), sdk version, region, and approximate client latency.
Mina K.: Repro steps for support ticket:
1) curl streaming example (replace tokens):
```
curl -s -N -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-stream-test","stream":true,"input":"<PROMPT>"}'
```
2) collect raw bytes (do not allow client library to auto-parse)
3) if invalid JSON appears, run local sanitizer and attempt re-ask with the stricter system instruction above.
Ashok: Ops-bot note: if this spawns >5 errors/min for the customer, auto-escalate SLA to eng-runtime and open a hotfix channel. :rotating_light:
support-bot: Logged support ticket #SUP-4621 and attached initial logs.
Sasha: One more pattern to try before full eng escalation: set the streaming chunk size to smaller pieces (reduce max_tokens per chunk) — sometimes models avoid appending debug when not finishing a chunk. Worth testing.
Jamie: TL;DR mitigation ladder: 1) client sanitizer (regex/last-brace) + quick parse attempt, 2) 1-2 re-asks with strict guard + small backoff, 3) proxy sanitizer / non-stream fallback, 4) model-variant check and eng escalation.
Mina K.: I'll propose the config changes to the customer (enable proxy sanitizer and temporary non-stream for that endpoint) and gather the raw streams + request IDs to escalate if it repeats. Thanks everyone :heart:
